subject: SLO & context-window checklist for Finex PoC – latency/throughput clarifications
messages:
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Simon Leary <simon.leary@finex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04T09:14:00Z
Subject: PoC follow-up: latency targets, streaming, and context-window notes

Hi Simon — great to meet this morning. Quick written recap and next steps so we have alignment before the PoC kick-off:

Summary from call
- Finex target: end-to-end user-perceived generation latency <= 350ms for interactive flows (p95) for typical 2–3 sentence prompts; ability to scale to 200 qps sustained during batch/off-peak periods.
- Streaming is required for the interactive UI so tokens should appear progressively in the client.
- Largest anticipated payloads: historic context up to ~18k tokens in long-search use case; typical chat flow will be ~1.2k input tokens + 300 output tokens.
- Security/compliance: standard SOC2 + IP protection; we will use hosted PoC with encrypted at-rest and in-transit.

Initial qualification notes and risks
- Context window: models supporting 32k tokens preferable, but larger input sizes increase KV-cache and can increase initial generation latency (first-token).
- Concurrency/throughput: continuous batching can reduce per-token cost but may add ~20–60ms to tail latency depending on queueing.
- Streaming behavior: chunk size and flush policy affect perceived latency; smaller increments reduce perceived latency but increase RPC overhead.

Requested artifacts (I attached a checklist)
1) 2–3 representative request examples (JSON) with tokenized sizes and expected output lengths — you can reply with those or drop in the Drive link. (see finex-sample-payloads.json attached)
2) Confirmation of SLO targets we should benchmark against (I documented the ones above; please confirm or adjust).
3) Any firewall/IP allowlist requirements for PoC.

Next steps
- Action: Finex to send 3 sample payloads (small/median/large) — due EOD Wed 3/11.
- Action: Redwood to provision a dedicated PoC instance (hosted) for Finex with streaming enabled and the 32k model profile; we will run a baseline benchmark and share a p50/p95 latency report — target by Fri 3/13.
- Meeting: follow-up technical sync with Vivek (CC'd) to deep dive on streaming and batching decisions — propose Tue 3/10 10am ET.

Attachments: SLO-checklist-Finex.xlsx, redwood-performance-baseline.pdf, finex-sample-payloads.json

Hi Simon — quick technical notes from my side to set expectations before we start benchmarking:

Measurement semantics
- Perceived (UI) latency: first-token-to-client is the key metric for interactive flows; for long-history search, full-response time is what matters. We will report both.

Streaming behavior details
- Flush window: 4-token flush windows are straightforward to model. Smaller flush windows reduce time-to-first-subsequent-token but increase gRPC/HTTP chunking overhead. Expect ~5–15ms overhead per flush on our hosted infra depending on network.
- Initial token: for very large context inputs (~18k tokens), first-token latency will be dominated by KV cache warm-up + attention setup. For a 32k model profile, plan for an additional 60–150ms on initial token for the largest payloads compared to small 1k-context prompts.

Context window and token limits
- For PoC, we recommend testing two profiles: 8k input / 4k output (fast path) and 32k input / 8k output (long-context). The 8k profile typically enables faster kernel paths and lower memory pressure — expect p95 generation latencies ~200–400ms for median payloads at modest concurrency (<=8).

Concurrency and throughput guidance
- Continuous batching: across concurrent requests, batching provides throughput gains but adds tail latency; at 200 qps with concurrency 16, expect batching-related queuing to add ~30–70ms to p95 unless you use smaller batching windows.
- Dedicated pools: recommending dedicated capacity for predictable p95 SLOs at your target qps. We'll size the pool after we see your sample payloads.

What Redwood will provide for the PoC
1) Synthetic benchmarks that mirror your 4-token flush client behavior and your sample payloads.
2) p50/p95/p99 latency breakdowns for first-token and final-token, token throughput, GPU util, and memory.
3) A short report highlighting any regressions and recommended batching/quantization knobs.

I'll bring detailed benchmarking scripts to the Tue 3/10 deep dive. If you want, we can also run an initial 30-min smoke test during our first PoC day to sanity-check streaming thresholds.
